name: Butter knife
description: A blunt table knife with a rounded tip, for spreading.
notes: A stainless table knife 210 mm long lying flat, held by its handle. The plastic knife rides here as the brief has variants do; the vegetable peeler has a different head and would suit its own model if it gains a peeling use.

name: Cast-iron skillet
description: A heavy cast-iron frying pan with a long handle and a lug on the far side.
notes: A skillet 270 mm across with a 140 mm handle and a helper lug, iron-cast with a coal-black hanging hole. It keeps a hammering quality for its weight; a melee profile is left for weapon tuning. The steel, copper and aluminium pans have their own drafts sharing this model.

name: Steel frying pan
description: A light stainless frying pan with a long handle.
notes: Shares the pan model, recoloured. The shared model's mass does not suit it; set its mass when the drafts are applied. Too light to bring hammering.

name: Copper frying pan
description: A copper frying pan with a long handle.
notes: Shares the pan model, recoloured. The shared model's mass does not suit it; set its mass when the drafts are applied.

name: Aluminium frying pan
description: A thin aluminium frying pan with a long handle.
notes: Shares the pan model, recoloured. The shared model's mass does not suit it; set its mass when the drafts are applied.

name: Pizza cutter
description: A steel cutting wheel on a plastic handle.
notes: A wheel 100 mm across on a fork and a plastic-red handle, 230 mm long, lying flat. A rolling wheel makes a poor cutting tool, so it brings no quality.

name: Child's bowl
description: A small bright plastic bowl made for a child.
notes: A bowl 120 mm across and 48 mm tall, plastic-orange with a plastic-white non-slip ring. The box counts the open bowl.

name: Plastic plate
description: A tough plastic dinner plate.
notes: A plate 256 mm across with a sloping rim, plastic-blue. The box counts the air over a flat plate; stacked plates take little room.

name: Drinking straw
description: A bendable plastic drinking straw.
notes: A red straw 6 mm across and 200 mm long with a ribbed elbow and its short end bent up. The box counts the bend.

name: Cooking pot
description: A steel stock pot with two handles and a lid.
notes: A pot 190 mm across and 130 mm deep with riveted loop handles and a domed lid with a plastic-black knob, steel-stainless. The aluminium pot has its own draft on this model.

name: Aluminium pot
description: A light aluminium pot with two handles and a lid.
notes: Shares the pot model, recoloured. The shared model's mass does not suit it; set its mass when the drafts are applied.

name: Canning pot
description: A 20 litre enamelled pot with a lid and a wire rack for jars.
notes: A canner 360 mm across and 260 mm tall, paint-drum-blue for dark enamel (no speckled enamel finish exists), with plastic-black handles and knob and steel-galvanised rack handles resting on the rim. Its size is a placeholder for a thing too big to carry far. The pressure cooker and clay pot oven ride here as the brief has variants do, though a locking lid and a heavy clay pot would each read better on their own model. The clay canning pot has its own draft on this model.

name: Clay canning pot
description: A large fired-clay pot with a lid, big enough to boil jars in.
notes: Shares the canning_pot model, recoloured clay-terracotta. A crafted pot would lack the wire rack and moulded handles; the shared model's mass does not suit it, so set its mass when the drafts are applied.

name: Copper pot
description: A tin-lined copper pot with brass handles and a lid.
notes: A pot 180 mm across and 140 mm deep: copper shell, steel-grey tin lining inside, brass handles and lid knob.

name: Hammered steel pot
description: A rough pot beaten out of a sheet of steel.
notes: Crafted, so it has no loot economy. A lopsided shell 200 mm across its crimped rim with hammer marks and a wire bail, drawn with 8 mm walls. The box counts the bail.

name: Hammered copper pot
description: A rough pot beaten out of copper sheet.
notes: Crafted, so it has no loot economy. The hammered pot drawn in copper with verdigris hammer marks and thinner walls; it is its own row rather than a recolour because its walls differ. The box counts the bail.

name: Rolling pin
description: A turned hardwood rolling pin with a handle at each end. Heavy enough to swing.
notes: A wood-birch pin 460 mm long with a 300 mm barrel 64 mm across, held by one handle. It would make a blunt club; a melee profile is left for weapon tuning.

name: Sippy cup
description: A child's plastic cup with two grips and a spill-proof spouted lid.
notes: A cup 70 mm across and 112 mm tall to the spout, plastic-blue with a plastic-white lid, spout to the front. The box counts the cup and grips.

name: Splatter screen
description: A round of fine steel mesh on a long handle, laid over a pan to stop spitting fat.
notes: A screen 290 mm across, 450 mm long with its handle, lying flat: a grid of steel-stainless wires at 12 mm pitch standing for the fine mesh, which no steel mesh finish shows, in a rolled rim with a plastic-black grip. sieving is a new quality name for sieve and strain uses. The box adds the handle's sweep.

name: Spoon
description: A stainless dessert spoon.
notes: A spoon 190 mm long lying on its back, steel-stainless with a steel-mirror well. The plastic spoons ride here as the brief has variants do. The ladle, whisk, garlic press, spatula, ice cream scoop and grater are distinct utensils; each would read better on its own model if it gains a use of its own.
